about.title: San Ramon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Ramon sits at the southern edge of Contra Costa County along I-680, and its roads carry a steady daily load of commuters moving between home, work and the freeway. In 2025, the city recorded 134 injury collisions, with 185 people hurt and one life lost. Public records show those crashes cluster along Bollinger Canyon Road, southbound I-680, Crow Canyon Road and San Ramon Valley Boulevard, and they tend to peak on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the workweek empties out at once. If you were injured in one of them, the weeks that follow can feel disorienting: medical appointments, calls from an adjuster, a car you cannot drive. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are a free service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened, and we will connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Contra Costa County and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case produces a recovery. You decide whether to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What Makes a Difference in a San Ramon Car Accident Case

items.title: Deadlines that can be shorter than you think
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident injury claim, but if a city, county or state agency is involved, you may have as little as six months to submit a formal claim. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible; your share of fault simply reduces the amount. That matters on busy stretches like Crow Canyon Road, where blame is often argued.

items.title: No cap, no upfront cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on I-680 southbound near San Ramon. Does it matter that it happened on a freeway?
items.answer: It can. Freeway crashes often involve multiple vehicles, higher speeds and sometimes questions about road conditions or state-maintained property, which can bring a public entity into the picture. When a government agency may share responsibility, California requires a formal claim within six months rather than the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate quickly whether that shorter deadline applies to you.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use your words to question your injuries or shift fault onto you. In the meantime, keep photos, the police report number, medical records and the names of any witnesses in one place.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost to use?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We are a free service that connects injured people in San Ramon and the rest of Contra Costa County with an independent personal injury attorney. The attorneys in our network handle car accident cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
